expr: (list (condition-case e (s-trim-left "  hi  ") (error (car e))) (condition-case e (s-trim-right "  hi  ") (error (car e))) (condition-case e (s-trim "\n\thi ") (error (car e))))
note: THE SILENT GAP AT PACKAGE LEVEL, which is the one the frontier probe calls the more interesting of the two. Emacs answers ("hi  " "  hi" "hi"); kg answers the three arguments UNCHANGED and raises nothing, because `string-match' on s-trim's patterns answers nil (phase26-anchor-s-trim-patterns) and s.el's `if' takes the else branch. `replace-match' is missing too and is masked by this: s.el never reaches the call. Both halves had to land before this case flipped, which is what made it the capability witness for the whole kg-side track rather than for either name alone. Both landed and it answers ("hi  " "  hi" "hi") now.
